item.title: [EU Observer] What kind of ECB is Europe getting after Lagarde?
item.description: Now that Paris and Berlin appear to have lined up Spanish central banker Pablo Hernández de Cos for the ECB presidency instead of his Dutch counterpart Klaas Knot, whether a dove or a hawk sits at the top may matter less than it seems, including for France.

item.title: [EU Observer] Xi keen to look ‘neutral’ on Ukraine at Shenzhen summit, as China risks spoiling EU relations by helping Putin to wage war
item.description: As Xi, Putin, and Trump gather in Shenzhen, Beijing is stretching its “neutral” pose to maintain a war‑fuelling trade lifeline for Moscow.

item.title: [EU Observer] Centrist and leftwing MEPs boycott rightwing NGO funding probe, which found no wrongdoing
item.description: As rightwing MEPs present their 71-page NGO funding report, centre and left-wing deputies stay away in protest, accusing the scrutiny group of bending parliament rules and sidelining their input.

item.description: Also, in tonight’s edition: Vučić from EPP, Iran-linked terror in the Balkans, and EU-UK summit latest

item.title: [EU Observer] EU auditors say rules ‘full of holes’ leave health at risk from toxic forever chemicals
item.description: Three eggs or a beef steak contain a dangerous amount of cancerous forever chemicals and yet it can take up to a decade before new harmful substances are banned under EU law.

item.description: European Commission must 'expedite' universal PFAS restriction, budget watchdog says

item.description: The loan will further integrate Ukrainian and European defence industries, Commission says

item.title: [Euractiv] How MSCA helped support Nobel Prize-Winning careers
item.description: Over its 30 years history, 25 Nobel Laureates have been affiliated with the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) as fellows, supervisors, or project coordinators. In this video, Anne L'Huillier and Stefan Hell share their experiences and reflect on the programme's contribution to scientific careers, international collaboration and groundbreaking research.

item.title: [EU Observer] Bridge Wars: Putin’s iconic Crimean Bridge destroyed despite ‘elite’ air-defences, but vital Kyiv bridge also close to collapse (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,728)
item.description: The sudden collapse of the Crimean Bridge’s key span, combined with precision Russian strikes on Kyiv’s lifeline bridges, threaten to choke off entire cities on both sides.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU opts for voluntary targets to secure key materials used in high-tech industries
item.description: The blueprint announced on Wednesday is the latest move by the EU executive to make the bloc's industrial base more self-reliant, but lacks a legal base.

item.title: [Euractiv] COP31: EU battles to get climate reports out sooner
item.description: Brussels is courting Beijing, whose backing would leave Saudi Arabia and India with few allies in the dispute

item.title: [EU Observer] Hungary digs up €17m in buried cash during probe into Orbán-era minister Seszták
item.description: Miklós Seszták, a minister under Viktor Orbán, is under investigation by Péter Magyar’s new anti-corruption body — and it took 12 treasury staff, five banknote-counting machines and eight hours to tally the €17m in buried cash linked to him.

item.title: [Financial Times] The only way out of populism is through it
item.description: The lesson of Britain and America is that bad ideas have to be tested to destruction

item.title: [EU Observer] EU Commission ‘confident’ that Bulgaria, Czech Republic, Hungary, and Slovakia will join new €45bn Ukraine loan
item.description: The EU Commission has come up with a new financing plan to fill Ukraine's €70bn funding gap next year, and thinks it has found a way to convince member states who want to opt-out by clearly separating civilian from military spending

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: Are EU sanctions against Russia really affecting the war effort?
item.description: The EU is preparing its 22nd package of sanctions against Russia. It is expected before the end of the year. This time, the measures are set to target more banks and crypto assets, as well as more ships from the so-called shadow fleet, those cargo that transport Russian oil, often under false flags. So, are those sanctions actually putting pressure on Russia?

item.title: [DW] Hashim Thaci's second conviction in The Hague reignites debate in Kosovo about justice and the Kosovo Specialist Chambers
item.description: Former President Hashim Thaci has been convicted of trying to influence witnesses in his war crimes trial. The conviction has reignited debate in Kosovo about the Kosovo Specialist Chambers, the court that convicted him.

item.title: [EU Observer] Rightwing MEPs switch attack from facts to ‘perceptions’, after a failed witch-hunt against NGOs in Brussels
item.description: After a year-long 'witch-hunt' that found no wrongdoing, rightwing MEPs are still pushing to choke NGO funding by leaning on vague “reputational risks” and “perceived” conflicts of interest, instead of hard evidence.

item.title: [EU Observer] UK sanctions on Israel leave EU unmoved, despite ‘man-made catastrophe’ in Gaza
item.description: In a voice from Gaza, Ahmed Abu Jami, a 28-year-old doctor, who lives in Khan Younis, told EUobserver via WhatsApp: "Things are bad, really, Gaza is descending into hell."

item.title: [EU Observer] EU asylum agency floats idea of foreign ‘processing centres’ to handle asylum claims
item.description: Innovative solutions is a catch all phrase that describes return hubs in Rwanda and Italy's controversial deal with Albania. Now it also applies to "process centres" for asylum seeker hopefuls.

item.title: [DW] Back to 1997: Russia wants NATO to roll back its eastern expansion
item.description: The Kremlin is reportedly calling on NATO to withdraw from large parts of Eastern Europe. What this would mean for the security of millions of Europeans — and what lies behind Russia's plan.

item.title: [EU Observer] France dethrones Sweden as EU gender equality leader — but overall progress is slowing
item.description: Europe still has a significant gender gap. It's in employment, in who takes care of children, in places of power. It's stronger in places like Cyprus and Bulgaria, while Spain and Denmark prioritised its gender politics. But full gender equality is still a distant goal, as Europe still lags behind pre-pandemic levels of parity.

item.title: [DW] Rights court rules Turkey must release jailed lawmaker Atalay
item.description: The European Court of Human Rights has called for the release of imprisoned elected lawmaker Can Atalay. Atalay has been in prison for almost five years despite rulings from the Turkish Constitutional Court.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU freezes €62.5m of Slovakia’s recovery funds over plans linked to ousted environment minister
item.description: Internal government warnings, downgraded wind plans and controversial zoning tweaks by ousted environment minister Taraba’s team now emerge at the heart of the Commission’s decision, exposing how months of behind-the-scenes manoeuvring may have sabotaged Slovakia’s own green transition money.

item.title: [DW] Students' List candidates take seats as Serbian parliament opens
item.description: Serbia's Student List's candidates have taken their oaths in the inaugural parliament session. As the new majority, they have 90 days to form a government.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU Commission again rebukes Temu over failure to stop illegal product sales, exposing Chinese giant to another hefty fine
item.description: Temu failed to take sufficient action to stop illegal or unsafe products being put on sale, the EU Commission has found preliminarily. It comes as part of a probe into the company's compliance with the Digital Services Act. The Chinese shopping website has disputed the latest findings.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Die Koalition der Wartenden: Europa blickt nach Shenzhen

item.title: [DW] Can the EU make it harder to trick consumers online?
item.description: The EU wants to curb subscription traps, misleading sales tactics and features that keep people scrolling. What would the proposed Digital Fairness Act change, and does it go far enough?

item.description: The first trilateral talks between Ukraine, the US and Russia in nine months have ended with an agreement on exchanging prisoners. Does this mark a genuine breakthrough and a step toward peace?

item.title: [DW] Hungary eases abortion restrictions in women's rights overhaul
item.description: The reforms mark a break the the conservative policies of former PM Viktor Orban. The controversial "heartbeat regulation" is to be scrapped and women are to be better protected against violence.

item.title: [DW] UK court convicts 2 Iranian men of spying on journalists
item.description: A London court has found two Iranian citizens guilty of surveilling reporters for a Persian-language television station critical of Iran's government. One was also convicted of planning a violent attack against them.

item.title: [DW] Despite restrictive abortion laws, Poland's 'Abortomat' — a locker that dispenses abortion pills — helps women who want to end a pregnancy
item.description: Abortion laws in Poland are very restrictive. Activists there have found a new way to help women wanting to terminate a pregnancy: the "Abortomat," a locker that dispenses abortion pills. But they face fierce opposition.

item.title: [DW] Ukraine: Zelenskyy says security deal could go to referendum
item.description: The US has broached the idea of Kyiv giving up the Donbas region in exchange for NATO membership, the Ukrainian president said.

item.title: [DW] Turkey uses espionage accusations to pressure government critics
item.description: The arrest of a German foundation's employee in Istanbul this week has put the focus back on pressure tactics used by the Erdogan administration. The arrest is far from the first of its kind.

item.title: [DW] Gen Z protests: Do Baby Boomers really have it better than young people?
item.description: Should young people in Germany be more worried about their future than Baby Boomers were in the 1980s and 1990s? Or should both generations take to the streets and protest together? DW checked the data.

item.title: [DW] The dangers of revising Europe's security architecture
item.description: Experts warn against revising Europe's security framework because they say it would mean granting Moscow its longstanding wish of renegotiating postwar security on the continent.

item.title: [DW] Czechia braces for massive protest against public media reform plans
item.description: A fast-tracked bill to cut public media funding has sparked strikes, rallies and fears for the independence of public broadcasting in Czechia. A massive protest is planned for Prague on Sunday.
